module Leaf::Editable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end
end

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

That confirms the root cause. Inside the sitting, `press` creates a leaf, and the leaf's `touch: true` saves the book again. That save clears `saved_changes`, so `saved_change_to_published?` is false when the commit callback runs. The unpublish path has no second save, so it still announces, and the condition also fires on unpublish, which is why unpublish announces.

The fix can't rely on `saved_changes` at commit time. Instead, the book should record its publication state during the sitting itself:
- on the first save in a transaction, note whether it was live at the start
- on every save, note whether it is live afterward
- at commit, announce only if it started unpublished and ended published
- on rollback, forget the state so a failed sitting leaves nothing behind

I'll write that now.

module Book::Announceable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_save :note_publication_during_sitting
    after_commit :announce_going_live
    after_rollback :forget_publication_during_sitting
  end

  private
    # A sitting is the transaction a save runs in. Other records saved along the
    # way (a page added to the book, say) touch the book again, which replaces its
    # saved_changes, so we can't ask saved_changes at commit time. Instead we note
    # whether the book was live when the sitting began, and whether it is live
    # after the latest save.
    def note_publication_during_sitting
      @published_at_sitting_start = attribute_before_last_save(:published) if @published_at_sitting_start.nil?
      @published_after_last_save = published
    end

    def announce_going_live
      went_live = @published_at_sitting_start == false && @published_after_last_save
      forget_publication_during_sitting

      AnnouncePublicationJob.perform_later self if went_live
    end

    def forget_publication_during_sitting
      @published_at_sitting_start = @published_after_last_save = nil
    end
end

module Book::Announceable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_save :note_publication_in_sitting
    after_commit :announce_going_live
    after_rollback :forget_publication_in_sitting
  end

  private
    # A sitting is the transaction a save runs in. It can save this book through
    # several in-memory copies (adding a page touches the book), and Rails runs the
    # commit callbacks on whichever copy saved last, which may not be the copy that
    # changed the publication. So the state is kept per sitting, not per copy.
    def publication_sittings
      ActiveSupport::IsolatedExecutionState[:book_publication_sittings] ||= {}
    end

    def note_publication_in_sitting
      sitting = publication_sittings[id] ||= { published_at_start: attribute_before_last_save(:published) }
      sitting[:published_now] = published
    end

    # Announce only if the sitting took the book from unpublished to published.
    def announce_going_live
      sitting = publication_sittings.delete(id)

      AnnouncePublicationJob.perform_later self if sitting && !sitting[:published_at_start] && sitting[:published_now]
    end

    def forget_publication_in_sitting
      publication_sittings.delete(id)
    end
end

module Book::Announceable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_save :note_publication_in_sitting
    after_commit :announce_going_live
    after_rollback :forget_publication_in_sitting
  end

  private
    # A sitting is the transaction a save runs in. It can save this book through
    # several in-memory copies (adding a page touches the book), and Rails runs the
    # commit callbacks on whichever copy saved last, which may not be the copy that
    # changed the publication. So the state is kept per sitting, not per copy.
    def publication_sittings
      ActiveSupport::IsolatedExecutionState[:book_publication_sittings] ||= {}
    end

    def note_publication_in_sitting
      sitting = publication_sittings[id] ||= { published_at_start: attribute_before_last_save(:published) }
      sitting[:published_at_end] = published
    end

    # Announce only if the sitting took the book from unpublished to published.
    def announce_going_live
      sitting = publication_sittings.delete(id)

      AnnouncePublicationJob.perform_later self if sitting && !sitting[:published_at_start] && sitting[:published_at_end]
    end

    def forget_publication_in_sitting
      publication_sittings.delete(id)
    end
end
